name: First Contact
definition: People encounter a genuinely unfamiliar intelligence and must build interpretation, communication, and policy while every assumption risks changing both sides.
negative_signals: aliens functioning only as invading monsters
familiar human culture with cosmetic differences
diagnostic_questions: Is understanding another intelligence the central problem?
Do communication choices change the relationship and stakes?

neighbors.distinction: First contact centers reciprocal interpretation, not discovery of place alone.
Contact promises possible understanding even when danger is real.

reader_promises.name: Meaningful otherness
reader_promises.description: Create differences in perception, value, embodiment, or time that affect interaction.

reader_promises.name: Consequential communication
reader_promises.description: Make signals, translation, and misunderstanding cause decisions rather than exposition alone.

roles.name: Interpreter
roles.description: Builds provisional meaning across scientific, linguistic, emotional, or embodied evidence.

roles.name: Policy maker
roles.description: Must act before understanding is complete and bears collective consequences.

roles.name: Contact intelligence
roles.description: Acts from its own constraints and revises its model of humanity.

conflicts: Mutual benefit versus incompatible survival needs

movements.name: Signal or encounter
movements.description: Establish undeniable intelligence and the first ambiguity it creates.

movements.name: Competing models
movements.description: Develop more than one interpretation and attach action consequences to each.

movements.name: Reciprocity
movements.description: Reveal that the other intelligence is also testing, misunderstanding, or adapting.

movements.name: Contact choice
movements.description: Choose a durable relationship under remaining uncertainty.

complications.name: Frame mismatch
complications.description: A valid signal is interpreted within the wrong unit, timescale, or social frame.

complications.name: Human factions
complications.description: Groups pursue incompatible policies before evidence becomes conclusive.

complications.name: Contact cost
complications.description: Communication itself changes biology, technology, memory, or political power.

twists.name: Different recipient
twists.description: The contact was directed toward another life form, machine, or future audience.

twists.name: Contact already occurred
twists.description: Current interpretation reveals an earlier unnoticed reciprocal encounter.

conclusions.name: Shared protocol
conclusions.description: Both sides establish limited reliable communication without eliminating difference.

conclusions.name: Protective distance
conclusions.description: Understanding leads to deliberate separation or delayed contact.

conclusions.name: Mutual change
conclusions.description: Contact transforms identities or institutions on both sides.

subversions: Make humans the harder party to interpret.
Resolve danger through a better question rather than a universal translator.
cliches_to_avoid: Aliens with one culture and one opinion
Instant translation without consequences or uncertainty
quality_checks: Otherness affects action, not only appearance.
The conclusion preserves difference while resolving the central contact choice.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Science Fiction
sources.contribution: Frames science fiction as an exploratory discussion capable of combining narrative modes.

sources.title: Science in Science Fiction: Making It Work
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Emphasizes credible extrapolation, internal consistency, and science ideas that advance plot.
